bundles.evidenceText: out of nothing nothing comes
bundles.rationale: The move asserts a general causal principle grounded in the intuition that something cannot come from nothing. No stated bridge specifically represents that causal principle, and it can be true without altering the actual-infinite, successive-addition, or personhood bridges. The pro motion bridge is the nearest competitor, but contact with only its causal premise does not support the complete compound motion conclusion.

bundles.evidenceText: there would be a difference in kind between the humdrum beginnings of things that we see every day and beginning of the universe
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that familiar rearrangements of existing material do not establish that the universe's introduction of material requires a cause. No stated bridge isolates that causal-principle inference, and the proposition can remain true without changing the credibility of the mapped finitude or personhood bridges. Attack on the pro motion bridge is excluded because one causal component does not constitute contact with the complete motion conclusion.

bundles.evidenceText: every thing that begins to exist has a cause
bundles.rationale: The move defends the causal principle for substances and applies it to the distinctive origin of the universe. The route map contains no causal-principle bridge, so this proposition is compatible with the truth or falsity of every stated actual-infinite, successive-addition, and personhood bridge. Support for the pro motion bridge is the nearest competitor, but a single causal premise cannot inherit contact with the complete compound motion conclusion.

bundles.evidenceText: that doesn't explain why a substance has to have a a cause for its beginning
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that describing nothingness as powerless merely restates rather than supports the claim that a substance must have a cause. That criticism can be true without making any stated finitude, Hilbert, countdown, or personhood bridge more or less credible. Attack on the pro motion bridge is excluded because the move challenges only an unmapped causal premise, not the complete motion-level conclusion.

bundles.evidenceText: there must have always been materiality
bundles.rationale: The move argues from the existence of something now and the impossibility of something coming from nothing to an eternal, beginningless material reality. That proposition directly makes less credible the pro central bridge's conclusion that the temporal series and universe began, so the polarity is attack. Support for the con central bridge is the nearest competitor, but the expressed inference directly denies the pro bridge rather than merely presenting the con route's general insufficiency claim.

bundles.evidenceText: it is impossible to form an actually infinite number of things by successive addition
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that successive addition cannot form an actual infinite and applies that restriction to the past-event series, concluding that it began. This cannot remain true without increasing the credibility of the pro subsidiary-2 bridge, so the polarity is support. The pro central bridge is excluded because the packet supplies the narrower successive-addition bridge receiving the exact proposition.

bundles.evidenceText: not something that exists in the real world
bundles.rationale: The move presents Hilbert's fully occupied infinite hotel and Hilbert's distinction between consistent infinite-set thought and real-world existence. This supplies support for the pro subsidiary-1 proposition that Hilbert-style concrete scenarios indicate metaphysical impossibility despite mathematical consistency. The pro central bridge is excluded because the evidence contacts the narrower Hilbert-scenario bridge rather than the entire past-finitude inference.

bundles.evidenceText: You can have proper parts that are equinumerous to the whole.
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that proper-part equinumerosity is simply a feature of infinite collections and that finite intuitions do not establish their real impossibility. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-1 bridge claiming Hilbert-style behavior reveals metaphysical impossibility. Support for con subsidiary-1 is excluded because the utterance is framed as a direct challenge to the pro bridge's inference, and direct attacks remain assigned to the bridge attacked.

bundles.evidenceText: Give up the most controversial one that an actual infinite number of things can exist
bundles.rationale: The move argues that metaphysical intuitions elicited by Hilbert's Hotel justify retaining Euclid's and Hume's principles while rejecting real actual infinities. That proposition cannot remain true without making the pro subsidiary-1 bridge more credible, so it supplies support. The pro central bridge is excluded because the expressed reasoning concerns Hilbert-style collections specifically, not the complete inference from a beginningless past to a beginning of the universe.

bundles.evidenceText: I don't see why I should make a big metaphysical concession when I could just change how I talk
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the apparent inconsistent triad can be resolved by using infinity-appropriate descriptions without denying actual infinities. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-1 inference from Hilbert-style behavior to metaphysical impossibility. Support for con subsidiary-1 is the nearest competitor, but the expressed force is a direct rejection of the pro bridge, so polarity and bridge identity remain attack on that bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: you can get any number from zero to infinity as result of these inverse operations
bundles.rationale: The move argues that subtracting equally numerous infinite subsets can yield arbitrarily different remainders and treats this as persuasive against concrete actual infinities. The proposition therefore supports the pro subsidiary-1 bridge concerning Hilbert-style scenarios and metaphysical impossibility. The pro central bridge is excluded because this is a specific hotel-based subtraction example, not the complete temporal-finitude inference.

bundles.evidenceText: I get out the right answer, there's no contradiction.
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that relative complements precisely identify which guests remain and eliminate the alleged contradiction in Hilbert's Hotel. That proposition directly makes the pro subsidiary-1 inference from the hotel's behavior to metaphysical impossibility less credible, so it is an attack. Support for con subsidiary-1 is excluded because the move directly rebuts the pro paradox argument, and a direct attack belongs to the bridge attacked.

bundles.evidenceText: identical quantities from identical quantities and you get non-identical remainders
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that relative-complement terminology merely conceals an arithmetic contradiction because identical infinite quantities yield non-identical remainders. This directly attacks the con subsidiary-1 proposition that Hilbert's unusual behavior does not establish impossibility. Support for pro subsidiary-1 is the nearest competitor, but the move is specifically a rebuttal of the con resolution, so the direct attack remains assigned to the con bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: I can't get to the end of the endless, but the countdown I can get to the end of the beginningless
bundles.rationale: The move asserts an asymmetry: an endless upward count has no end, whereas a beginningless countdown can have the present as its end. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-2 claim that a beginningless countdown cannot be completed. Support for con subsidiary-2 is excluded because the proposition is expressed as a direct diagnosis of the gap in the pro inference, so the attack belongs to the pro bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: if he could finish by today, he should have finished by any point in the infinite past
bundles.rationale: The move argues that any earlier point already follows infinitely many counting moments, so permitting completion today implies completion at every prior point and contradicts the stipulated countdown. This directly attacks the con subsidiary-2 claim that a beginningless countdown can coherently reach its present end. Support for pro subsidiary-2 is excluded because the move directly answers and rejects the con bridge's stated asymmetry.

bundles.evidenceText: It doesn't mean that he should have done or he would have done.
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that infinitely much elapsed time is necessary but not sufficient for completion, so the counter may coherently have been at two yesterday and finish today. That diagnosis directly attacks the pro subsidiary-2 inference that a beginningless countdown cannot reach the present. Support for con subsidiary-2 is excluded because the utterance specifically rejects the pro argument's conditional inference, making it a direct attack on that bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: why does he finish just now rather than yesterday since an infinite number of seconds had already elapsed?
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that even a restricted principle of sufficient reason demands an explanation for completion today rather than yesterday after infinitely many elapsed seconds. This directly makes the con subsidiary-2 account of a coherently completed beginningless countdown less credible, so it attacks that bridge. Support for pro subsidiary-2 is excluded because the move is framed as a rebuttal to the con diagnosis rather than a fresh statement of the whole pro bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: I can give partial explanations
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the counter's preceding numeral and fixed rate provide an adequate partial explanation of why he finishes today, without requiring an ultimate explanation. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-2 objection that the completed beginningless countdown remains inexplicable or impossible. Support for con subsidiary-2 is excluded because the inferential force is a direct answer to the pro bridge's completion objection.

bundles.evidenceText: no less mysterious by answering
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that citing the immediately preceding numeral is irrelevant to the contextual causal question and leaves today's completion just as mysterious. This directly attacks the con subsidiary-2 proposition that the present end of a beginningless countdown is coherently explained. Support for pro subsidiary-2 is excluded because the move is a targeted rebuttal to the con account, so direct-attack specificity fixes the con bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: you cannot live past midnight and yet no Grim Reaper can strike you down
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that a non-well-founded descending Grim Reaper series produces an explicit contradiction and generalizes this to successively traversing such a series. This supports the pro subsidiary-2 proposition that a beginningless successive series cannot be completed. The pro subsidiary-1 bridge is excluded because the example concerns temporal successive traversal, not Hilbert-style static infinite collections.

bundles.evidenceText: prior to that we have some kind of Swinburne, Padgett, Mullins view about there being a non-metricated past eternity
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that even granting the Hilbert and successive-addition arguments may establish only a finite beginning of metric time while leaving a non-metric past eternity. This directly attacks the pro central conclusion that the temporal series and universe began. Support for con central is excluded because the move is formulated as a limitation on the pro finitude inference, and direct attacks belong to the bridge limited.

bundles.evidenceText: it looks suspiciously like a point, which looks like timelessness, like eternity
bundles.rationale: The move argues that any pre-metric state must also lack linear geometry and consequently resembles a timeless point rather than a genuine beginningless temporal series. This directly attacks the con central claim that a coherent beginningless-past alternative remains available. Support for the pro central bridge is excluded because the move concedes amorphous-time language and specifically challenges the con alternative rather than restating the full actual-infinite inference.

bundles.evidenceText: sort of impersonal indeterministic causation
bundles.rationale: The move argues that an indeterministic impersonal mechanism could originate the universe at a particular time and looks relevantly similar to libertarian personal choice. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-3 inference that personal agency is required where an impersonal cause cannot produce a first effect. Support for con subsidiary-3 is excluded because the alternative is introduced specifically to challenge the pro personhood inference, so the direct attack belongs to the pro bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: it doesn't make sense to have a changeless personal uh agent
bundles.rationale: The move argues from the essentially dynamic character of conscious experience that a changeless, disembodied mind outside a changing causal order is incoherent. That challenges a necessary premise of the pro subsidiary-3 claim that a personal agent can originate the first universe, so the polarity is attack. The con subsidiary-3 bridge is excluded because the move offers no impersonal indeterministic origin model; it directly contests personal-agent coherence.

bundles.evidenceText: there is no incoherence in the notion of a timeless person
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the freezing illustration supports the coherence of unchanging consciousness and that a timeless person is conceptually possible. This supplies support for a necessary premise of the pro subsidiary-3 bridge, under which a personal agent can originate a temporally first universe. Attack on the con central bridge is excluded because the proposition specifically concerns personal-agent coherence, not the general availability of beginningless or impersonal alternatives.
